stem:
In a physiology laboratory, a 22-year-old student injects current into a neuron and depolarizes its membrane from -70 mV to -60 mV, but no action potential follows. A second, stronger injection depolarizes the membrane to -55 mV and a full action potential fires.

The critical difference at -55 mV is the opening of which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Leakage channels, initiating a steady sodium drift inward
options.misconception: Randomly gated background channels are being treated as a threshold device.
options.explanation: Leakage channels open and close at random to help set the resting potential; the regenerative upstroke begins only when voltage-gated Na+ channels open at threshold.

options.label: B
options.text: Voltage-gated sodium channels, initiating a full action potential
options.misconception: None; threshold is the voltage at which voltage-gated Na+ channels open.
options.explanation: At about -55 mV the activation gates of voltage-gated Na+ channels open, Na+ rushes in, and the action potential proceeds all-or-none to its peak near +30 mV; subthreshold depolarizations die out.

options.label: C
options.text: Voltage-gated calcium channels, initiating neurotransmitter release
options.misconception: The terminal's release machinery is being confused with the axon's firing trigger.
options.explanation: Ca2+ entry at the synaptic end bulb couples the arriving action potential to vesicle fusion; it does not set the axon's -55 mV firing threshold.

options.label: D
options.text: Voltage-gated potassium channels, initiating repolarization of the action potential
options.misconception: The repolarizing channel is being cast as the trigger of the upstroke.
options.explanation: Voltage-gated K+ channels open later, near the peak, to drive repolarization; threshold is defined by Na+ channel opening.

options.label: E
options.text: Sodium-potassium pumps, initiating active restoration of the gradients
options.misconception: A slow housekeeping transporter is being treated as the fast trigger of firing.
options.explanation: The Na+/K+ pump maintains gradients over seconds to minutes; it does not open at -55 mV and plays no role in the millisecond upstroke.

context: Learning objective: define threshold. Depolarization to about -55 mV opens voltage-gated Na+ channels; anything less fails to fire, and anything reaching it produces the same full action potential (all-or-none).
imageCaption: Neuron RMP, threshold AP, refractory period, saltatory conduction, EPSP/IPSP summation.
